background: The Toronto-Dominion Bank is Canada's second-largest bank, funded by Canadian and US deposits and lending on Canadian mortgages and to businesses, with a large US retail bank along the east coast that has been under a regulatory asset cap after its anti-money-laundering failures.
synthesis: Rated A+ on average across all three, the weakest of them at A, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 23 Oct 2024, the bank's standing remains strong despite its US compliance failings. CET1 of 14.3% is in the top quarter of Canadian banks, though it has fallen 0.6 points since 30 Apr 2025, with figures to 31 Jul 2026. The weak spot is conduct and operations: the newest flagged item, on 7 Oct 2026, is a former employee's guilty plea to money laundering, and others report customer data breaches.
